facts.statement: Lonchognathosaurus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous in the Lianmuqin Formation of Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: Lonchognathosaurus is a genus of dsungaripterid pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Aptian-Albian-age Lower Cretaceous Lianmuqin Formation of Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: The genus Lonchognathosaurus was named in 2004 by Michael Maisch, Andreas Matzke, and Sun Ge.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2004 by Michael Maisch, Andreas Matzke and Sun Ge.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Lonchognathosaurus acutirostris.
facts.quote: The type species is Lonchognathosaurus acutirostris.

facts.statement: The genus name means "lance-jaw lizard" in Greek, referring to the animal's pointed jaws.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Greek , "lance", , "jaw" and , "lizard", in reference to the fact that it is a reptile with pointed jaws.

facts.statement: The specific name acutirostris means "needle snout" in Latin.
facts.quote: The specific name means "needle snout" in Latin.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, found near Urumqi in the southern Junggar Basin, consists of the front of a skull and lower jaws from a large individual with an estimated total skull length of 400 mm.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Lonchognathosaurus, SGP 2001/19, was found near Urumqi in the southern Junggar Basin, the front portion of a skull and lower jaws that came from a large individual; the estimated length of the complete skull was about 400 mm (15.75 in).

facts.statement: The tip of the upper jaw was slender and needle-like, formed by the premaxilla bones.
facts.quote: The point of the upper jaw, composed of the premaxilla bones, was slender and had a needle-like tip.

facts.statement: Each upper jaw had only eight teeth and a straight lower margin, unlike the strongly curved margins seen in other pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Each maxilla only had eight teeth, and the bottom margin of the upper jaw was straight (unlike in other pterosaurs where it is strongly curved).

facts.statement: The skull featured a sagittal crest with grooves and a concave leading margin.
facts.quote: A sagittal crest was present, with grooves and a concave leading margin.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis classifies Lonchognathosaurus as a member of the family Dsungaripteridae and the sister taxon to Dsungaripterus.
facts.quote: The genus was, after a cladistic analysis, classified as a member of the Dsungaripteridae, as the sister taxon to Dsungaripterus.

facts.statement: Brian Andres argues that Lonchognathosaurus is a junior synonym of Dsungaripterus weii.
facts.quote: According to Brian Andres Lonchognathosaurus is a junior synonym of Dsungaripterus weii.

facts.statement: In 2021, Augustin et al. described postcranial elements from the Lianmuqin Formation that confirmed the validity of the genus and provided new anatomical information.
facts.quote: However, in 2021, postcranial elements referrable to Lonchognathosaurus, confirming the validity of the genus and providing new information on the anatomy of this pterosaur, were described from the Lower Cretaceous Lianmuqin Formation (China) by Augustin et al..

facts.statement: The time range for Lonchognathosaurus is estimated from 137.05 to 100.5 million years ago, spanning the Valanginian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Albian (137.05 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Averianov et al. (2022) identified a wing metacarpal fragment from the Ilek Formation in West Siberia as possibly belonging to Lonchognathosaurus due to its near identity with the type species.
facts.quote: Averianov et al., (2022) described a distal fragment of the wing metacarpal from the Lower Cretaceous Barremian-Aptian age Ilek Formation in West Siberia, Russia and identified it as cf. Lonchognathosaurus sp., since it is "nearly identical to the wing metacarpal of Lonchognathosaurus acutirostris."

rejected.statement: David Hone argued in 2017 that the species could not be distinguished from Noripterus.
rejected.quote: David Hone on the other hand, argued in 2017 that the species could not be distinguished from Noripterus.
